query: Flow-cytometric quantification of macrophage efferocytosis using fluorescently labeled apoptotic cells
title: Efferocytosis assay to quantify the engulfment and acidification of apoptotic cells by macrophages using flow cytometry
markdown:
## Protocol: Flow-cytometric quantification of macrophage efferocytosis using fluorescently labeled apoptotic cells

### Overview

This protocol outlines the flow-cytometric quantification of macrophage efferocytosis using fluorescently labeled apoptotic Jurkat cells. The procedure involves preparing specific culture media and buffers, inducing apoptosis in Jurkat cells followed by dual-labeling with Hoechst 33342 and pHrodo-Red, differentiating Bone Marrow-Derived Macrophages (BMDMs) from mouse long bones over seven days, performing the efferocytosis assay at defined ratios and time points, and finally collecting and analyzing the cells via flow cytometry to quantify engulfment.

### Materials/Reagents

Jurkat cells, L-929 cells, Mouse bone marrow, RPMI-1640 basal medium, DMEM basal medium, HI-FBS, HEPES, L-glutamine, Penicillin-streptomycin, Sodium pyruvate, EDTA, DPBS, Staurosporine, Hoechst 33342, pHrodo-Red, Annexin V conjugate (Alexa Fluor 647), Propidium Iodide (PI), Annexin binding buffer (10 mM HEPES, 140 mM NaCl, 2.5 mM CaCl2, pH 7.4), CellStripper, L-929 cell-conditioned media.

### Equipment

Class II Biological Safety Cabinet (BSC), CO2 incubator (37°C, 5% CO2), Centrifuge, Flow Cytometer (e.g., BD LSRFortessa with UV/violet 405 nm and red 532 nm lasers), FCS Express software, 150-mm tissue culture dishes, 50-mL conical tubes, 5-mL round bottom polypropylene/polystyrene test tubes, 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes, 40 μm cell strainers, 26G needles, 10-mL syringes, Ophthalmic scissors, Beebee bone scissors, Forceps, 6-well and 12-well non-TC-treated plates.

### Safety & Sterility

Clean surgical tools (ophthalmic scissors, Beebee bone scissors, forceps) by spraying with 70% ethanol and allowing evaporation. Maintain sterility for all procedures and reagents/tools after initial bone dissection. Work in a Class II BSC for sterile steps. Avoid direct light exposure during pHrodo and Annexin V staining. Use IACUC-approved methods for mouse euthanasia.

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation Phase

1. Prepare Jurkat cell culture media by mixing the following reagents: 50 mL HI-FBS (10%), 5 mL HEPES (10 mM), 5 mL L-glutamine (2 mM), 5 mL Penicillin-streptomycin (100 U/mL), 5 mL Sodium pyruvate (1 mM), and 430 mL RPMI-1640 basal medium to achieve a total volume of 500 mL. Filter sterilize the media and store at 4°C for up to one month. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare L-929 cell culture media by mixing the following reagents: 50 mL HI-FBS (10%), 5 mL L-glutamine (2 mM), 5 mL Penicillin-streptomycin (100 U/mL), and 440 mL DMEM basal medium to achieve a total volume of 500 mL. Filter sterilize the media and store at 4°C for up to one month. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare PM isolation buffer by mixing the following reagents: 50 mL HI-FBS (10%), 2 mL EDTA (2 mM), and 448 mL DPBS to achieve a total volume of 500 mL. Filter sterilize the buffer and store at 4°C for up to one month. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Prepare Macrophage culture media by mixing the following reagents: 100 mL L-929 cell-conditioned media (20%), 50 mL HI-FBS (10%), 5 mL L-glutamine (2 mM), 5 mL Penicillin-streptomycin (100 U/mL), and 340 mL DMEM basal medium to achieve a total volume of 500 mL. Filter sterilize the media and store at 4°C for up to one month. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
5. Prepare FACS buffer by mixing the following reagents: 10 mL HI-FBS (2%), 2 mL EDTA (2 mM), 5 mL HEPES (10 mM), 5 mL Sodium pyruvate (1 mM), and 478 mL DPBS to achieve a total volume of 500 mL. Filter sterilize the buffer and store at 4°C for up to one month. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
6. Clean surgical tools, including ophthalmic scissors, Beebee bone scissors, and forceps, by spraying them with 70% ethanol and allowing the ethanol to evaporate completely. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
7. Prepare L-929 cell-conditioned media by culturing L-929 cells at 37°C in 5% CO _2 incubator and collect conditioned media. a. Thaw a cryovial containing 1 × 10 ^7 cryopreserved L-929 cells. b. Plate cells in 25 mL L-929 cell culture media in a 150-mm tissue culture (TC)-treated dish. c. Allow the cells to grow until they reach around 90% confluence (typically in 2-3 days), then split the cells into five 150-mm dishes (1:5 split ratio). d. Once cells in the five 150-mm dishes reach around 90% confluence, split the cells to a total of 100 150-mm dishes (1:20 split ratio). e. When cells reach around 90% confluence, replace the media with 25 mL fresh media. f. After an additional 48 h culture, harvest conditioned media without disturbing the cells, and proceed to filter the media using a 500-mL vacuum filter/storage bottle. g. Freeze aliquots of L-929 cell-conditioned media in 50-mL conical tubes and store at −80°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->
8. Seed Jurkat cells in non-TC-treated flasks at a density of 0.5 × 10^6 cells/mL. Split the cultures at a 1:4 or 1:5 ratio every 3 days or when the density reaches 2.2-2.6 × 10^6 cells/mL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S08 -->

## Apoptotic Cell Induction and Labeling

### Induction Phase

1. Generate apoptotic Jurkat cells by treating Jurkat cells with 0.5 μg/mL staurosporine in RPMI-1640 basal medium at a density of 2.5 × 10^6 cells/mL. Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 in 50-mL conical tubes placed on a rack with caps slightly open for 2.5 hours. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
2. After the 2.5-hour incubation, aliquot cells for apoptosis rate assessment. Transfer 200 μL of cell suspension containing approximately 0.5 × 10^6 cells to a 5-mL round bottom polypropylene test tube or a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube. Set this tube aside while proceeding to the next step. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->

### Labeling Phase

1. Perform Hoechst labeling. For the remaining cell suspension, directly add Hoechst 33342 at a working concentration of 2-4 μM to label nuclear DNA. Return all tubes, including the reserved 200 μL aliquot, to the incubator for another 0.5 hours at 37°C and 5% CO2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S01 -->
2. Wash apoptotic cells (ACs) after apoptosis induction and Hoechst labeling. Centrifuge tubes at 550 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C to pellet cells and aspirate the supernatant. Resuspend the pellet in 50 mL RPMI-1640 basal medium to wash away Hoechst dye. Centrifuge again at 550 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C to pellet cells and aspirate the supernatant. Note: Because the cells are apoptotic, a higher speed is required to pellet them effectively. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S02 -->
3. Perform pHrodo labeling. Resuspend the pellet in RPMI-1640 basal medium at a density of 20 × 10^6 cells/mL. Add 4 μL of 10.2 mM pHrodo-Red stock per mL of cell suspension. Stain for 25 minutes at 20°C-25°C in a Class II BSC. Avoid direct light exposure during staining. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S03 -->
4. Complete washing and resuspension. Fill the tube with 50 mL RPMI-1640 basal medium to wash the pellet, ensuring complete removal of residual staurosporine and labeling dyes. Resuspend the pellet in a small volume of DMEM basal medium + 10% HI-FBS and count the cells. Based on the total cell count, resuspend the labeled ACs in DMEM basal medium + 10% HI-FBS at a final concentration of 10 × 10^6 cells/mL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S04 -->

## Apoptotic Cell Preparation and Labeling

### After the 2.5 h incubation

1. After the 2.5-hour incubation for apoptosis induction, aliquot cells for the assessment of apoptosis rate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S34 -->
2. Transfer 200 μL of cell suspension containing approximately 0.5 × 10^6 cells to a 5-mL round bottom polypropylene test tube or a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S35 -->
3. Set the tube aside while working on the next step (Hoechst labeling). [1] <!-- protocol-step:S36 -->
4. Perform Hoechst labeling. For the remaining cells, directly add Hoechst 33342 to the Jurkat cell suspension at a working concentration of 2-4 μM to label nuclear DNA. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S37 -->
5. Return the tubes, including the 200 μL cell aliquot in the 5-mL round bottom polypropylene test tube, to the incubator for another 0.5 hours at 37°C and 5% CO2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S38 -->
6. Wash ACs after apoptosis induction and Hoechst labeling. Centrifuge the tubes at 550 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C to pellet cells and aspirate the supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S39 -->
7. Resuspend the pellet with 50 mL RPMI-1640 basal medium to wash the Hoechst dye. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S40 -->
8. Centrifuge at 550 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C to pellet cells and aspirate the supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S41 -->
9. Perform pHrodo labeling. Resuspend the pellet with RPMI-1640 basal medium at a density of 20 × 10^6 cells/mL for pHrodo staining. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S09 -->
10. Add 4 μL stock of 10.2 mM pHrodo-Red per mL of cell suspension and stain for 25 minutes at 20°C-25°C in the Class II BSC. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S10 -->
11. Fill the tube with 50 mL RPMI-1640 basal medium to wash the pellet, completely removing residual staurosporine and labeling dyes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S11 -->
12. Resuspend the pellet in a small volume of DMEM basal medium + 10% HI-FBS and count the cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S12 -->
13. Based on the total number of cells, resuspend labeled ACs with DMEM basal medium + 10% HI-FBS at a concentration of 10 × 10^6 cells/mL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S13 -->

### Quality control for apoptotic rate

#### Branch A: Apoptosis Rate Assessment

1. Assess apoptosis rate. Centrifuge the aliquoted 200 μL apoptotic Jurkat cell suspension (approximately 0.5 × 10^6 cells) at 550 × g for 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S01 -->
2. Directly add 4 mL ice-cold DPBS and centrifuge at 550 × g for 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S02 -->
3. Resuspend cells with 400 μL annexin binding buffer (10 mM HEPES, 140 mM NaCl, and 2.5 mM CaCl2, pH 7.4). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S03 -->
4. Transfer 100 μL of cell suspension to a 5-mL round bottom polystyrene test tube, then add 5 μL of Annexin V conjugate (Alexa Fluor 647). Incubate for 15 minutes at 20°C-25°C, avoiding direct light exposure. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S04 -->
5. Stop the staining by adding 400 μL annexin binding buffer. Keep the stained cells on ice from this point forward. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S05 -->
6. To simultaneously assess necrotic cells, add 10 μL propidium iodide (PI) solution to the 500 μL cell suspension and vortex for 3 seconds. Incubate on ice for 10-15 minutes for staining and conduct analysis by flow cytometry. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S06 -->

## BMDM Preparation

### Day 0

1. Euthanize mice by cervical dislocation under anesthesia or by IACUC-approved methods. Place euthanized mice in a supine position and spray with 70% ethanol. Separate the long bones: use forceps to grasp the skin at the lower quadrant of the ventral abdominal region right above the hip line, make a small incision with an ophthalmic scissor, extend the incision down the leg to the ankle, pull back the skin to expose the hind limb, remove muscle and connective tissues, separate the hip joint and Achilles tendon to cut out the leg bone (including femur, knee, and tibia), and place the leg bone in a dish with Dulbecco's Phosphate-Buffered Saline (DPBS) to separate the tibia and femur at the knee joint. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: It is important to maintain the integrity of joints at the ends of the long bones during dissection. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
2. Remove remaining muscle and connective tissues from the bones and rinse the femur and tibia with DPBS. Transfer bones from both legs to a new dish with ice-cold DPBS containing 100 units/mL penicillin-streptomycin in a Class II biological safety cabinet (BSC). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: All procedures and reagents/tools must be sterile after this point. From each mouse, two femurs and two tibias can be obtained from the hind limbs. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
3. Collect bone marrow (BM) in DMEM basal medium. Place a 40 μm cell strainer on top of a 50-mL conical tube held upright in a rack. Attach a 26G needle to a 10-mL syringe and draw up to 10 mL DMEM basal medium. Using forceps to grasp the femur or tibia, remove the condyles (rounded, knuckle-like ends) of one side of the bone using a Beebee bone scissor to expose the metaphysis. Flush and collect BM cells: hold the bone above the strainer with the open end facing down, gently push the syringe needle through the intact end of the bone into the medullary cavity, and slowly flush the BM into the 50-mL conical tube through the 40 μm strainer (1-2 mL media should be sufficient per bone). Repeat for each femur and tibia per leg (total 4 bones per mouse); repeat flushing until the bone is white, indicating all marrow has been flushed out. Use another 10-15 mL DMEM basal medium to flush the BM on the strainer to disaggregate cells so they pass through while tissue debris remains; obtain a total volume of approximately 20-30 mL from one mouse. Centrifuge at 4°C, 400 × g for 5 minutes. Aspirate the supernatant to obtain the cell pellet and resuspend the pellet in complete macrophage culture media. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
4. Differentiate BM cells to BMDMs. On Day 0, seed BM cells in non-TC-treated 6-well plates at 2 × 10^6 cells per well in 2.5 mL macrophage culture media. Critical: Using petri dishes or non-TC-treated flasks and plates is essential so that differentiated BMDMs can be lifted for flow cytometry-based analysis. Note: Red blood cell lysis is generally not required for BMDM differentiation; if desired, perform it using commercially available lysis buffer according to manufacturer's recommendations. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->

### Day 5

1. On Day 5, BM cells should adhere and cover the dish sufficiently. Supplement the culture with 1 mL macrophage culture media per well. Note: If obvious floating dead cells are present, replace 2.5 mL fresh macrophage culture media to remove them; otherwise, supplementing 1 mL media per well is generally sufficient. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->

### Day 7

1. On Day 7, for successful differentiation, expect to obtain 0.8-1.0 × 10^6 BMDMs per well of a 6-well plate, with cells appearing approximately 80% confluent. BMDMs are ready for the efferocytosis assay at day 7. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->

## Collection and Analysis

### 2 h

1. At the desired time for efferocytosis is reached, wash cells with DPBS 3-5 times at 20°C-25°C. Gently shake the plate during washing to remove unengulfed ACs. **Note:** Take care not to dislodge macrophages. Remove DPBS, add CellStripper (2 mL per well for 6-well plate or 1 mL per well for 12-well plate). Place the plate in 5% CO _2 incubator at 37°C. It usually takes ∼10 min to lift the cells. Take the plate out at ∼5 min and observe to avoid over digestion which will compromise cell viability. If needed, gently pipet to dislodge macrophages. **Alternatives:** CellStripper has a non-enzymatic formulation and is often used when maintaining cell surface proteins and antigens is critical, or when working with sensitive cell types. Trypsin can also be used and typically requires a shorter incubation time compared to CellStripper. **Note:** Lifting PMs requires a shorter incubation time compared to BMDMs. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S01 -->
2. When macrophages are lifted, stop the reaction by adding 2 mL DMEM basal medium + 10% HI-FBS. Transfer the suspension to 5-mL round bottom polystyrene test tubes or other tubes compatible with the flow cytometer. Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 minutes to pellet the macrophages. Aspirate the supernatant to obtain the pellet, resuspend the pellet (from one well of a 6-well or 12-well plate) in 300 μL FACS buffer. Keep the tubes on ice before analysis by flow cytometry. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S02 -->
3. The Hoechst dye can be detected using UV laser or violet laser (405 nm laser). The pHrodo-Red dye can be detected using red laser (532 nm). **Note:** Data shown in [Figures 3] and [4] were obtained using BD LSRFortessa Cell Analyzer using the violet laser and red laser. We observe that BD LSRFortessa gives better separation of positive versus negative populations. While other flow cytometers typically yield reliable separation, variations may be observed. It is generally recommended to use the same flow cytometer for a given project. Aim to collect 10,000 single cells, but no less than 2,000 single cells, for reliable quantification ( [troubleshooting 1] , [2] , and [3] ). **CRITICAL:** Flow cytometry analysis should be done within one hour or up to two hours upon collection to ensure optimal cell viability. Analyze data using FCS Express or other software. Following [Figures 3] and [4] for gating strategies for the analysis of BMDM and PM efferocytosis, respectively. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S03 -->

## Efferocytosis Assay

### 1 h

1. Perform the efferocytosis assay. Each well of a 6-well plate of BMDM culture at day 7-9 usually contains 0.8-1.0 × 10^6 BMDMs. Subject BMDMs to different levels of apoptotic cell (AC) burden by performing the assay at different AC:BMDM ratios (e.g., 3:1, 5:1, and 10:1). Calculate the amount of ACs per well and respective volume (e.g., for a 5:1 ratio, calculate approximately 4-5 × 10^6 ACs per well). Aspirate the BMDM culture media. Replenish the well with DMEM basal medium + 10% HI-FBS; based on the calculation, add the respective amount of AC suspension to make a final concentration reflecting the chosen AC:BMDM ratio in a total volume of 1 mL. Take extra care not to swirl the plate to ensure even distribution of ACs on the BMDMs. For peritoneal macrophages (PMs), each well of a 6-well plate usually contains 0.8-1.0 × 10^6 PM, and the same calculation applies. Return the plate to the incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 for efferocytosis. Different time points can be assessed to obtain a time-response curve (generally 45 min, 60 min, and 90 min). In general, 60 min is most often used to assess engulfment. To also assess acidification, use 90 min to allow extra time for engulfed cargos to undergo lysosomal acidification. If predicting reduced efferocytosis due to manipulation, extending incubation time or increasing AC burden may help identify deficiencies. Conversely, if predicting enhanced efferocytosis, a shorter incubation time may be chosen. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->
